title: Null Run tower environment kits: Ashbell Foundry, Boneglass Conservatory, Skyhotel Service Well

seam_behavior.walls: All eight wall tiles are RGB 128x128 and seamless on both axes. Opposite edge rows and columns are exactly equal. Tiles 07 and 08 are landmark accent panels; each wraps independently and the pair is an authored adjacent motif, not a continuous split image.
seam_behavior.flats: All four flats are RGB 64x64 and seamless on both axes. Opposite edge rows and columns are exactly equal.
seam_behavior.props: All props are RGBA 96x128 cut-outs with at least three transparent pixels on every edge and feet/bases at the bottom. They are not tiled and have no opaque rectangular backdrop.

selection.notes: Suggestions only. Codex owns seeded selection and native integration. Use one kit as a whole-run or whole-tier identity; do not mix kits per room. Keep walls 07 and 08 together.
selection.suggested_seed_use: Derive the set from the run seed as a separate choice from map layout, so the same layout can be replayed with a different kit.

floor_variation.notes: Metadata only; Codex implements any variation. Flats 01-04 are a complete floor/ceiling set and should not be mixed with another kit.
rules: flats/02 is the utility or service floor for plant rooms, trenches and back-of-house.
flats/04 is the lit or fixture ceiling; it is never a floor.
Vary floors by room function, not by per-tile random substitution.

integration_status.native_loader: The reviewed rogue/environments.py PACK_IDS tuple and catalogue length check currently name the three previously reviewed sets. Codex must add these IDs and MOB/3D wiring before native loading.

sets.name: ASHBELL FOUNDRY
sets.description: A vertical bell foundry inside a dead furnace stack: riveted soot iron, pale firebrick arches, oxidised bronze and verdigris chain galleries. Casting bells hang in open shafts beside black furnace mouths, and a counterweighted lift cage links suspended maintenance balconies. The building is a working machine that has been left running without anyone to pour. Every ascent is physical: stairs, ladders and a chain lift move through real floor openings, never a painted backdrop.

landmark.name: The Ninth Bell
landmark.description: A cracked ninth casting bell hangs from a crown gimbal in the open lift shaft, flanked by a bronze cage and a counterweight chain. The bell crown and the lift cage are authored as adjacent landmark panels; the bell is the thing the whole tower is arranged around.

service_lamp.description: A three-legged iron hook stand holding a bronze ladle cup of standing furnace light, with a short chain, ash tray and a heat-scorched shade. Small freestanding floor fixture.
service_lamp.silhouette: tripod, curved hook, deep cup; reads as a ladle, not a box.

cable_shrine.description: A squat cast-iron chain drum with a coiled chain mound, a hanging hook and counterweight, three bronze studs and a grease pot. Freestanding foundry utility object.
cable_shrine.silhouette: low drum with an asymmetric chain coil and a hanging hook.

directory_sign.description: A two-post cast frame carrying a tilted soot board with three bell-shaped order plaques of different sizes, a bronze direction arrow and a top chain. Landmark wayfinding object with solid feet.
directory_sign.silhouette: tall A-frame with three hanging bell plaques.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material and architecture guidance only. The kit makes no collision, light, AI or audio claim. Warm furnace accents are sparse so bright binding rings and projectiles stay legible. Use one kit per run.
sets.impossible_detail: The ninth bell has a casting seam on both faces and no clapper; the lift counterweight rises when the cage is empty. Visual fiction only.

verticality.fall_recovery: staged chain galleries and a sand bed at the pit

sets.name: BONEGLASS CONSERVATORY
sets.description: An abandoned indoor woodland nursery grown past its glass: bone-white tiled walls, black peat beds, pale fungal trees, root cages and watering gantries under a dead glasshouse roof. Vegetation descends from the floors above in long curtains, and every growth chamber is empty in a way that looks recently vacated. Unease is carried by silhouette and negative space rather than gore: a pale trunk where a person should be, a cage of roots around nothing, a watering arm still pointing at a dry bed.

landmark.name: The Root Cage
landmark.description: A hanging cage woven from white roots around a black vertical void, suspended beneath the descending canopy. The paired landmark panels are the cage (07) and the canopy curtain with its growth lamps (08). The cage is empty; the roots continue upward past the frame.

service_lamp.description: A curved root stem rising from a mossy ceramic pot, ending in a drooping translucent seed pod with a pale fungal glow, a copper tag and loose tendrils. Small organic floor fixture.
service_lamp.silhouette: single curved stem and a hanging pod; no straight post.

cable_shrine.description: A verdigris watering standpipe with a cross tap, a wide watering rose and a pressure bulb, half swallowed by white roots and a black peat mound. Freestanding nursery utility object.
cable_shrine.silhouette: cross-shaped pipe, round rose, irregular root mass.

directory_sign.description: A leaning bone trellis lectern with a shallow black seed tray, three hanging seed labels and root-wrapped legs. Landmark indexing object with a solid base.
directory_sign.silhouette: slanted trellis with a cradle of tags, not a flat board.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material and architecture guidance only. Pale surfaces are kept mid-value so bright binding rings remain visible; no bloom, fog volume or animated growth is implied. Use one kit per run.
sets.impossible_detail: The root cage has no entrance and its shadow falls upward onto the canopy. The watering rose drips into a bed that is already full. Visual fiction.

verticality.fall_recovery: soft peat beds and staggered planter shelves

sets.name: SKYHOTEL SERVICE WELL
sets.description: The back-of-house innards of a late-night observation hotel: staggered room balconies around a deep service atrium, luggage dumbwaiters, rain-streaked glass, blue-grey night and dirty amber signs. Guest floors are readable as stacked rectangles while the service core cuts a separate vertical route through them. The architecture is deliberately orthogonal and staggered, not radial: landings step around corners, balconies overhang one another, and the lift is the only warm thing in the shaft.

landmark.name: The 33rd Floor Lift
landmark.description: A brass service lift with one door panel ajar on amber light and an indicator that carries a floor mark which does not exist. The paired landmark panels are the lift door (07) and a cutaway of the staggered balcony atrium with the hanging luggage cage (08).

service_lamp.description: A brass floor lamp on a stable foot, with a rectangular amber shade, a rain hood and a hanging luggage tag. Small freestanding hotel fixture.
service_lamp.silhouette: slim post, broad rectangular shade, hanging tag.

cable_shrine.description: A squat brass and steel luggage winch with a large spoked wheel, a cable spool, a hanging suitcase and a three-button call plate. Freestanding service utility object.
cable_shrine.silhouette: low body dominated by one big wheel and a hanging case.

directory_sign.description: A tall brass-framed directory with three staggered miniature balcony shelves, amber floor ticks, a large direction arrow and a rain hood. Landmark wayfinding object with two solid legs.
directory_sign.silhouette: stepped three-shelf frame under a projecting hood.

sets.gameplay_notes: Cosmetic material and architecture guidance only. Blue-grey surfaces and dirty amber signage keep the value range away from binding-ring colours. No live reflections, rain physics or light animation is claimed.
sets.impossible_detail: The lift indicator shows a floor between 32 and 33; the directory has the same floor twice with different arrows. Visual fiction, not a secret door.

verticality.fall_recovery: balcony setbacks, linen chute shelves and a laundry net
